ICC is a road taking, not a zoning cap: class b.

comment: The shortfall comes from phasing. Phase I (32 TH) was approved and graded in 2003, when only 2.59 net ac was RT-12.5 (32 = 12.5 x 2.59); the 2003 opinion deferred the R-90 part until the SMA. After G-827, Phase II added 21 TH on 1.56 ac (13.5 du/ac). No 2005 cap. The 2004 Upper Rock Creek plan is internally inconsistent: the text says R-90 to RT-12.5, but the bullet says 'Reclassify ... to the RT-10 Zone ... The precise number of units ... determined as part of a required site plan review' (dl_g3/fraley_UpperRockCreekMasterPlan2004.pdf p.29). The mapped zone governs. The 2003 duplex plan kept the project under the 50-unit MPDU trigger.

comment: Open point settled: the Ten Mile Creek Limited Amendment sets 1 du/ac as the base, with MPDUs beyond 12.5% added on top only within the impervious cap. The 2014 code's RNC optional method (MPDU development) caps density at 1.22 units/acre of usable area (dl_g3/creekside_Ch59_2014_council_approved.pdf, Sec. 4.3.5.E, p.4-25), which is 1.0 x 1.22. The project gives exactly 12.5% MPDUs, so it takes no bonus; 394 is the right base. Class b is my inference: impervious cover is 5.9% against a 6% cap and the buildable land is a ridge crest, but no document says units were cut for this. The schools test held the first approval to 187 units for a time only.
